question: A sponsor wants to deploy a new Claude-powered feature to all users in every region simultaneously on day one. What rollout approach should be recommended instead, and why?
options: A) Recommend delaying the launch indefinitely, since no rollout strategy can reduce risk for AI-powered features.
B) Recommend the simultaneous global launch as proposed, since phased rollouts add no measurable risk-reduction benefit.
C) Recommend a phased rollout to a small user segment first, so issues can be caught and addressed before scaling to everyone.
D) Recommend launching only in the region with the least usage data, since regional differences do not affect quality.
correct_answers: C) Recommend a phased rollout to a small user segment first, so issues can be caught and addressed before scaling to everyone.
explanations: Incorrect. Indefinite delay is unnecessary; a phased approach allows launch to proceed while managing risk.
Incorrect. Phased rollouts are a standard risk-reduction practice; claiming no benefit contradicts common deployment guidance.
Correct. A phased or pilot rollout to a limited audience lets the team observe real-world performance and fix issues before exposing the full user base to them, reducing overall risk.
Incorrect. Regional usage patterns and data characteristics can affect performance, so ignoring them is not sound rollout planning.
